recommendation: Keep the FHIR-13615 audit as no-change. Handle FHIR-54545 separately when R6 Ready_to_Apply work is in scope, including replacing the DiagnosticReport.identifier v2 mapping, updating basedOn mappings, and removing the DiagnosticReport identifier note as directed there.
issue_request: FHIR-13615 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 OO change request to update DiagnosticReport.identifier's HL7 v2 mapping so it explains how to handle unique and non-unique filler identifiers.
initial_application: Git commit b434255fbc971400e662a6a7409206826628b33b (GF#13615) changed the DiagnosticReport spreadsheet mapping from OBR-51 to text distinguishing globally unique filler IDs from non-globally unique filler/placer identifiers combined with the universal service ID. The 2021 source rework commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 migrated that same mapping into source/diagnosticreport/structuredefinition-DiagnosticReport.xml.
additional_context: DiagnosticReport is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current StructureDefinition source still contains the FHIR-13615 mapping on DiagnosticReport.identifier. The originating Zulip ORU^R01 thread confirms the rationale: when a filler order number is not globally unique, a group/order identifier may need to be combined with the test code. A later R6 issue, FHIR-54545, is Resolved - change required / Ready_to_Apply and would replace this mapping by moving V2 order numbers to basedOn, but it is a separate unapplied R6 decision outside this seed's applied/published scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope source already carries the historical FHIR-13615 mapping, and applying the later FHIR-54545 replacement under this seed would conflate two separate work-group decisions.

related_jiras.note: R6 Ready_to_Apply decision would supersede the FHIR-13615 mapping by moving V2 order numbers to basedOn, but it is not Applied/Published and was not decided in this seed.
